newsitem.title: USA: Rubin denies U.S., Japan talked of capping dollar.
newsitem.headline: Rubin denies U.S., Japan talked of capping dollar.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Tuesday that he had accomplished what he wanted in his meetings with Japanese officials last week and denied suggestions that the two sides had discussed trying to cap the dollar's advance.
"If they (the Japanese) are (trying to do that), they didn't discuss it with us," Rubin told reporters on his way back here from a six-day trip to Asia.
"We never discussed exchange rates at all," added Rubin, who met Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka in Tokyo last Friday.
After the meetings, Hashimoto was quoted by Japanese officials as agreeing with Rubin that Tokyo must have growth led by domestic demand and avoid a big rise in its current account surplus.
"We accomplished what we had hoped to accomplish from these meetings," Rubin said.
Japan is counting on a potentially risky strategy of massive deregulation and a sharp budget squeeze to keep its economy moving forward and its trade surplus in check.
While in Tokyo, Rubin reserved judgment on whether the policy mix would work or whether Japan would need to take further measures in the coming months to spur economic growth.
Rubin said on Tuesday that Hashimoto clearly was committed to pressing ahead with structural reforms and had the support of business leaders for his efforts.
But he added that the reforms, like any change, would be politically difficult to carry out.
Rubin said he also discussed the problems besetting Japan's banking industry in his meetings last week in Tokyo.
"They talked about their view that they have this set of issues under control," the Treasury chief said, without saying where he stood on the issue.
The dollar has risen sharply in the wake of Rubin's meetings in Tokyo last week partly because of market perceptions that he will not do anything to stem its advance.
